summary: The appeal arises from a partition suit concerning properties allegedly acquired by R.M. Patil. The Trial Court dismissed claims for partition and accounting of rents but granted a prohibitory injunction in favor of the second plaintiff. The High Court set aside this judgment, allowing partition of items 1 to 4 while excluding item 5 (library books) as valueless and permitting the first defendant to retain them. The appellant challenged the decision on grounds of non-joinder of necessary parties, exclusion of joint family properties, and adverse possession via ouster. Respondents argued the suit pertained only to self-acquired properties of R.M. Patil and that no joint family properties were excluded. The Supreme Court considered issues of coparcenary rights, ouster, impleadment, and equitable distribution under Article 142.
legal_provisions_cited: Article 142 of the Constitution of India
final_judgment: Appeal disposed of with no order as to costs.
